importance_rationale: First public, comparatively benchmarked DECtp launch — Olsen, Glorioso, and Hughes presenting the debit-credit benchmark from the Plaza Hotel, July 1988 — that put tps and $/tps into rigorous procurement language and provably embarrassed IBM's DB2 TP performance and scaling. The TPC was formed within roughly a month as the direct institutional response.
relevance_rationale: The four pillars introduced that day — tps as the unit of measure, $/tps as the procurement metric, RDBMS as the assumed TP substrate, and scale-as-a-procurement-requirement — are still load-bearing in 2026 across OLTP procurement, TPC-derived benchmarks, and cloud-database price-performance comparisons.
prescience_rationale: Six inflection-point bets all won on the timelines implied: focus on $/tps for two decades, RDBMS as TP benchmark standard, scaling counts, standardized TPC benchmarks, DEC TP business doubled in a year, TPC became undisputed arbiter. See kastner-author/notes/dectp_prescience_rationale_2026_06_13.md for full argument of record.
